title: Are All Odd Zeta Values Transcendental?
description: Formalizes the open question: are all odd zeta values ζ(2k+1) transcendental? Proves even zeta transcendence (from Lindemann), axiomatizes Apéry, Rivoal, and Zudilin theorems, and establishes the full implication hierarchy: transcendence conjecture ⟹ irrationality conjecture ⟹ all known results.

overview.historicalContext: The even zeta values ζ(2k) = rational × π^(2k) have been fully understood since Euler (1734) and Lindemann (1882): they are all transcendental. The odd zeta values ζ(2k+1) remain deeply mysterious. Not a single one has been proved transcendental. Even the weaker question of irrationality is largely open: Apéry (1978) proved ζ(3) irrational in a tour de force, Rivoal (2000) showed infinitely many odd ζ are irrational, and Zudilin (2001) pinpointed ζ(5,7,9,11) as containing at least one irrational. But beyond these partial results, specific odd zeta values remain out of reach.
overview.problemStatement:
**Open Conjecture**: For all k ≥ 1, ζ(2k+1) is transcendental over ℚ.

Not a single odd zeta value is known to be transcendental. Even ζ(3) — the only specific odd zeta value known to be irrational — has unknown transcendence status.

**Known hierarchy**:
- Transcendence conjecture ⟹ Irrationality conjecture
- Irrationality conjecture ⟹ Apéry theorem
- Irrationality conjecture ⟹ Rivoal theorem
- Irrationality conjecture ⟹ Zudilin theorem
overview.text: A 187-line formalization of the arithmetic landscape of odd zeta values. Defines zetaValue(s) = ∑ 1/n^s and proves the closed forms ζ(2) = π²/6 and ζ(4) = π⁴/90 from Mathlib. Four deep results are axiomatized: Lindemann's theorem (π transcendental), Apéry's theorem (ζ(3) irrational), Rivoal's theorem (infinitely many odd ζ irrational), and Zudilin's theorem (one of ζ(5,7,9,11) irrational). States the transcendence and irrationality conjectures, then proves a chain of structural implications showing the transcendence conjecture recovers all known results. Two sorry targets on even-zeta transcendence are set up for automated proof search via Aristotle.
overview.proofStrategy:
The formalization proceeds in layers:

**Layer 1 (Mathlib)**: Closed forms ζ(2) = π²/6, ζ(4) = π⁴/90 from hasSum_zeta_two/four.

**Layer 2 (Axioms)**: Four deep results not in Mathlib — Lindemann, Apéry, Rivoal, Zudilin.

**Layer 3 (Conjectures)**: The transcendence and irrationality conjectures as Prop definitions.

**Layer 4 (Structure)**: Proved implications forming the hierarchy:
- transcendence ⟹ irrationality (via Transcendental.irrational)
- irrationality ⟹ Apéry (specialization at k=1)
- irrationality ⟹ Rivoal (via Set.infinite_of_injective_forall_mem)
- irrationality ⟹ Zudilin (specialization at k=2)

**Layer 5 (Sorry targets)**: Even-zeta transcendence from Lindemann — awaiting Mathlib transcendence API for algebraic closure under field operations.
keyInsights: The even/odd divide in zeta values is one of the starkest in number theory: complete understanding vs near-total mystery
Rivoal's theorem is best formalized using Set.Infinite rather than quantified Finset bounds — cleaner and more compositional
The full implication chain (transcendence → irrationality → all known results) is provable without sorry
Even-zeta transcendence needs: if π is transcendental, then π^n/q is transcendental for n ≥ 1, q ∈ ℚ×. This requires Mathlib's algebraic closure infrastructure.

Zudilin's 4-way disjunction (one of ζ(5,7,9,11) irrational) is the tightest known finite explicit bound — improving it to a 3-way or 2-way disjunction remains open and would require fundamentally new ideas in Padé approximation

conclusion.summary: This formalization maps the frontier of odd zeta value arithmetic. Four deep axioms capture the state of the art: Lindemann, Apéry, Rivoal, Zudilin. The key structural result conjecture_implies_all_known shows the transcendence conjecture is a single hypothesis that, if proved, would subsume all existing partial results. The two sorry targets on even-zeta transcendence are routine Mathlib glue (algebraic closure under rational scaling and powers) suitable for automated proof search.
conclusion.implications:
**If the transcendence conjecture were proved**: All known partial results follow as corollaries. More importantly, the techniques would likely revolutionize analytic number theory — current methods (hypergeometric series, Padé approximants) cannot even prove irrationality of ζ(5) individually.

**For formalization**: The even-zeta transcendence proofs await Mathlib's algebraic number theory infrastructure — specifically, that rational multiples of transcendental powers remain transcendental. Once Lindemann-Weierstrass enters Mathlib, pi_transcendental can be upgraded from axiom to theorem.
openQuestions: Is ζ(3) transcendental? (The most accessible individual case)
Is any specific odd zeta value transcendental?
Are ζ(3), ζ(5), ζ(7), ... algebraically independent over ℚ?
Can the Ball-Rivoal method be refined to prove individual irrationality results?
